fantasy: Alone between the posts, you are the last line no attacker can get past — read the windup, pick your side, and keep the clean sheet alive.
core_loop: A round starts with 3 lives -> the AI attacker steps up and winds up a shot from a changing angle, distance and speed, the windup growing shorter as the round goes on -> the player reads the windup and taps the left, centre or right zone to dive -> a correctly timed dive is a save that extends the streak and nudges the next shot harder; a missed or late dive is a concede that resets the streak and costs a life -> the round ends when the player saves the round's shot target (win) or lives hit zero (loss) -> the result card shows the streak, save accuracy and personal best, and the player retries the same round or advances to the next, harder round built from the same tuned shot data, not new content.
pillars: The windup always tells the truth: every shot is readable before it arrives
Every concede is a late or wrong read, never bad luck
Back between the posts within one second of a concede

engine.rationale: Depth is part of the read: the attacker's run-up, the windup lean and the ball's closing speed and angle are only legible from a 3D goal-mouth camera. Three.js with low-poly procedural geometry and vertex colours keeps the load budget close to a 2D title; textures and PBR materials are deliberately excluded.
engine.camera: Behind-the-goal chase camera at keeper eye height, framing the attacker's run-up and the full goal mouth; no player camera control.

features.name: Goalkeeper dive control
features.description: A single tap control: the player taps the left, centre or right zone over the goal mouth to dive or move the keeper there, timed against the attacker's windup.
acceptance: Tapping a zone commits the keeper to a dive toward that zone within the shot's reaction window.
The keeper cannot change zone once committed; one tap resolves one shot.
Strategy MVP: A single tap control: the player moves, dives and blocks to deny every shot.

features.name: AI attacker and shot variety
features.description: One computer-controlled attacker occupies the shooting spot and fires at goal from varying angles, distances and speeds, telegraphed by a windup whose duration shrinks as difficulty rises.
acceptance: Each shot's windup visibly leans toward the side the ball will go before the ball is kicked.
Shot speed, angle offset from centre and windup duration are drawn from the current difficulty step's data, not hand-placed per shot.
Only one attacker and one ball are ever in play.

features.name: Save streak and lives
features.description: A save extends the player's defensive streak and raises the next shot's difficulty; a concede resets the streak and costs a life.
acceptance: A save increments the streak and tightens the next shot's windup and widens its angle range by the round's per-save step.
A concede sets the streak to 0 and removes one life.
A round starts with 3 lives.

scope.progression_terminal: Progression is the personal best (longest save streak and highest round reached). The ramp is bounded by 3 tuned difficulty rounds using the same shot set - there is no content treadmill to feed.

session.structure: A round lasts roughly 45-60s across its shot target. The first session drops straight into play with no menu, round 1 at its easiest tuning. Later sessions open on the title screen with the personal best visible. A session is roughly 2 rounds back to back; it ends at a natural stopping point - a round win advancing to a harder round, or a loss with retry/continue offered - rather than being cut off.
session.end_condition: The player sets a new personal-best streak or round reached, or fails to improve across three rounds.

retention.return_reason: I know I can hold a clean sheet longer if I read the windup better next time.
retention.progression_loop: Progression is the personal best (longest save streak and highest round reached). The ramp is bounded by 3 tuned difficulty rounds - there is no content treadmill to feed.

placements.trigger: On a round-ending concede (lives empty) after at least one save has been made, offer one continue that restores a life and keeps the current streak

monetization.economy: No currency. The rewarded continue is the only economic action.

progression: Skill only: win round 1 (reach its shot target) to unlock round 2's harder tuning; win round 2 to unlock round 3's harder tuning. There is no currency or unlock track - only the save streak and the round reached.
difficulty: Round 1, shots 1-3: windup 900ms, shot speed 14 units/s, angle range +/-25 degrees from centre, straight drives only, so a first-time player sees the full windup before committing. After each save within a round: windup tightens 40ms and speed rises 0.4 units/s, down to the round's floor. Round 2 (after winning round 1): base windup 700ms, speed 16 units/s, angle range +/-35 degrees, near-post pins added. Round 3 (after winning round 2): base windup 550ms, speed 18 units/s, angle range +/-45 degrees, chips and dipping shots added. Assist: after two concedes in a row with no save between them, the next shot's windup resets to the round's base value instead of its tightened one.
controls: Tap one of three zones over the goal mouth - left, centre, right - timed to the attacker's windup, to dive or move the keeper that way; one tap commits one dive per shot. This is the only control: on desktop a click on the same zone is the equivalent action, and there is no separate keyboard scheme, per the strategy's one-control-scheme decision.

ux.onboarding: Guided first save. The dive is one idea - zone, timed to windup; the first attacker's windup is slow and exaggerated, and the correct zone glows once before the first shot arrives.
ux.accessibility: Every windup has a visual tell independent of audio, so the game plays muted - which also covers the large share of portal traffic that plays with sound off. The zone a shot favours is never signalled by colour alone; an arrow/lean cue accompanies it. Text is at least 16 CSS px at the design resolution. A reduced-motion setting (and prefers-reduced-motion) disables camera shake and flash feedback on a concede.

art_direction: Night-match floodlights: a near-black stadium bowl, a stark white goal-mouth under hard floodlight, and one hot accent colour that marks 'the danger side' of every shot. Identity kit 'floodlight'. Hard 2px strokes with a soft floodlight glow on the ball and net; pill buttons only for the single primary action (Play/Retry/Next round), everything else square-cornered like scoreboard signage.
audio_direction: Library stadium ambience bed (crowd murmur) plus short library SFX for windup, save and concede, all compressed and loaded after first play so audio never delays time to first play. Every windup and shot cue has a visual twin, so the game reads with sound off.

Shot speed, angle offset from centre and windup duration are drawn from the current round's difficulty step.
Only one attacker and one ball are in play at a time.

mechanics.description: A save extends the player's streak and nudges the next shot's parameters harder; a concede resets the streak and costs a life.

A concede sets streak to 0 and removes one life.

A win offers the next, harder round built from the same tuned shot data.
A loss shows the result card with streak, save accuracy and personal best.

The core loop produces an unforced desire to retry within one 120-second session
The rewarded placement reads as a favour rather than an interruption
